children: China and Hong Kong stocks tumbled in early trade on Friday, tracking a global tech rout as fears of tighter AI regulation and a slowdown in the sector rattled investors.
Tech led the drop, with startup board Star 50 Index
both down more than 5% at the open before narrowing some of the losses.
In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng
was down 1.6% while the Hang Seng Artificial Intelligence Index

Overnight in the US market, the tech-led Nasdaq notched its deepest one-day drop since "Liberation Day" in April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced sweeping tariffs. The drop  wiped out trillions in market value on fears of more AI scrutiny after Democrats won big in US midterm elections.
The fear trade carried on in early Asia hours, with South Korea's KOSPI
plunging more than 8% and Japan's Nikkei
falling 5%. The South Korean move triggered exchange circuit breakers for a 20-minute trading halt.
